evidence.location: §4 RC3 criteria, RC3-C4, read with §2.3 Baseline and §10 RC-D4
evidence.observation: RC3-C4 reads "key survives inserting a rule above another and inserting a fact above another", while §2.3 defines the key as "(address, canonical JSON of the offending row)" and RC-D4 answers the id-less case with "key by positional address, `addressing: positional` tells the caller it is unstable". Inserting a rule above an id-less constraint changes its positional `constraint_ref`, so the key changes for exactly the class RC-D4 concedes is unstable, and standing rows would be re-reported as new.

concerns.recommendation: Scope RC3-C4 to constraints with a declared `id` (the class O4 makes a stable key), and either make `--baseline` refuse id-less constraints with a stated exit code or add a criterion pinning that positional-keyed rows are only comparable within one model revision, so a run can fail the criterion.
concerns.title: RC3-C4 asserts a key stability the plan itself denies for positional addresses

evidence.location: §2.4 Vacuous acceptance (RC4), read with §3 dependency note and §0 rule 7
evidence.observation: §2.4 says "the payload records that the option was used" and RC4-C3 says "the payload records the option", but no §3 artifact row names the schema or key that carries it, §3 says "RC4 and RC5 are independent and may run in any order", and rule 7 says "New meaning goes in version 15 only". The flag is described as run-wide, not restricted to `--rule-ids`, so RC4 landing before RC1 would have to record the option in an already-frozen report version.

concerns.recommendation: Name the schema and key for the allow-vacuous record in the §3 artifact table, then either add an RC1 -> RC4 edge to the §3 graph or state that the record lives outside the frozen report variants; add an RC4 criterion that existing-version bytes are unchanged when the flag is absent and that the record appears only where rule 7 permits.
concerns.title: RC4's payload record of --allow-vacuous has no named home and can breach the frozen-variant rule

evidence.location: §5 first bullet, read with §4 RC1-C3 / RC2-C3 and completion predicate 1
evidence.observation: §5 claims "Report versions 3-14 keep their bytes (rule 7)" and predicate 1 claims "Version 7 bytes are unchanged for every existing input", but the only byte criteria are "RC1-C3: without `--rule-ids`, output bytes for the rf1 sem-check goldens are unchanged" and "RC2-C3: version 7 output for the same input is unchanged". §9 names no suite covering versions 8-14, including the 10/13 re-projections §2.1 depends on, and "every existing input" is not a set a gate can enumerate.

concerns.recommendation: Either name the existing goldens or suites that pin versions 8-14 and add them to RC1's focused gate in §9, or add a criterion stating that any golden moving outside version 15 fails the gate; if neither is available at the baseline, narrow §5 and predicate 1 to version 7 and say plainly that the rest is unpinned.
concerns.title: The versions 3-14 freeze claim has no falsifiable criterion beyond the v7 rf1 goldens

evidence.location: §4 RC2-C4 and RC3-C5, read with the §1 O15 row and §0 rule 2
evidence.observation: "RC2-C4: time bound over 2,000+ edges" and "RC3-C5: validation order pinned; time bound over 2,000+ rows" state no bound value, and the only sizing datum is "| O15 | 2,047 edges / 209 components checked in 2.5 s | issue 94/92 | claim | RC2, RC3 time bounds |", which the plan itself classifies as a claim not reproduced at 33d1db49, while rule 2 says "Each ships a time-bound test".

concerns.recommendation: Give each criterion a numeric bound with its fixture size and measurement condition, or defer the number to the phase spec the way RC6 defers its gate; have the RC2/RC3 specs record a baseline timing of the synthetic 209-component, 2,047-edge fixture so the bound derives from a measurement made in this repository rather than from O15.
concerns.title: RC2-C4 and RC3-C5 cannot fail as written: no numeric bound, and the only sizing datum is an unreproduced claim

evidence.location: §2.1 fourth bullet ("RC1 D3"), read with the §6 risk-table last row and §4 RC1-C4
evidence.observation: §2.1 says "`--rule-ids` refuses them in this milestone (RC1 D3)" and §6 makes that refusal the entire control for "Redacted values make a baseline key meaningless", namely "`--rule-ids` (and so `--baseline`) refuses redaction-policy models", but RC1's only refusal criterion is "RC1-C4: `--rule-ids` with any other arm exits 64". §10 contains no RC1-D3; its RC-D3 is "Acyclic rows: one per group, or one per in-group edge?", so the cross-reference resolves to nothing, and completion predicate 1 states unconditionally that `--rule-ids` emits version 15.

concerns.recommendation: Add an RC1 criterion naming the exit code and message for redaction-policy and temporal models under `--rule-ids`, a matching RC3 criterion for `--baseline`, repair or delete the dangling "(RC1 D3)" reference, and qualify predicate 1 with the same exception so the control in §6 is actually gated.
concerns.title: The load-bearing refusal of redaction and temporal models has no criterion and cites a decision id that does not exist

evidence.location: §3 dependency note, read with §4 RC4-C1, the §6 band row and §10 RC-D6
evidence.observation: §3 says "RC4 and RC5 are independent and may run in any order" while §6 says "RC3/RC4 extend `band()`, the one implementation". RC-D6 proposes "exit 4; no novelty claim for that constraint" when either run leaves an alethic constraint unchecked and RC4-C1 says "vacuous-only run exits 0 with the option, 2 without", but no line states the outcome of `--baseline --allow-vacuous` when the head or base run contains vacuous verdicts.

concerns.recommendation: Add one line to §2.3 or §2.4 fixing the combined outcome (whether --allow-vacuous suppresses RC-D6's exit 4, and whether a vacuous verdict in the base run counts as undecided for novelty), and note in §3 that whichever of RC3 or RC4 lands second must re-run the other's gate because both edit `band()`.
concerns.title: The --baseline x --allow-vacuous outcome is unspecified although both phases edit the single band() implementation

evidence.location: §4 heading "### RC6: Documentation (docs only)", read with the §9 RC6 row
evidence.observation: Every feature phase carries a budget, e.g. "### RC1: Declared identity, report version 15 (about 180 source, 350 test lines)", but RC6 is headed only "### RC6: Documentation (docs only)" and its §9 gate reads "unresolved; candidate `tests/test_documentation_tutorials.py`", while completion predicate 6 requires "a worked example that runs (RC6)". No phase in §4 states what happens when its budget is exceeded.

concerns.recommendation: Give RC6 a budget (pages plus the tutorial fixture size) and a stop condition, and either fix `tests/test_documentation_tutorials.py` as its gate now or attach the deferral to a decision id in §10, so predicate 6's "runs" is measurable at the phase gate; add the same stop-condition rule to RC1-RC5.
concerns.title: RC6 has neither a budget nor a resolved gate, and no phase names a stop condition

evidence.location: Header paragraph on PR 99, read with the §9 RC1 gate row
evidence.observation: The header says "PR 99 (open) repairs 24 failing tests on main; RC1's focused gate runs after that PR merges or names the pre-existing failures it inherits (RC-D1)", and the gate is "uv run pytest -q tests/test_rc1_*.py tests/test_schema_sync.py tests/test_checker_families.py tests/test_rf1_semantic_pins.py". Nothing requires that exact command to be run and recorded before RC1's changes land, so a red gate cannot be attributed to either cause.

concerns.recommendation: Require the RC1 spec to capture the verbatim pre-change run of that exact gate at the merge base (the RC-D1 fallback), and state that RC1-C3's byte comparison is judged against that recorded baseline, so inherited failures can be neither read as regressions nor waved through.
concerns.title: RC1's focused gate has no recorded pre-change baseline, so inherited failures cannot be told apart from regressions

evidence.location: §4 RC5-C2, read with the §3 artifact row "population source" and §1 O13
evidence.observation: RC5-C2 says "the three spellings of the enum reduce to one home (rule 5)", but the §3 row names two homes: "| population source | `src/gnd/schema/population.schema.json` (+ skill copy), `src/gnd/population.py` |", and O13's third site "`src/gnd/extract/projection.py:278`" does not appear in the table at all, although §5 says "`gnd-extract` keeps writing `agent-output`; RC5 does not change it".

concerns.recommendation: Name the single normative home for the source enum and state how the remaining sites are derived or sync-pinned (the `remedy` row already models this with "sync-pinned copy"), add `extract/projection.py` to the §3 row, and reword RC5-C2 so a run can fail it, for example that the literal appears once and a sync test pins the others.
concerns.title: RC5-C2's "one home" contradicts the §3 row that names two homes and omits the third spelling

evidence.location: §3 artifact row "declared address", read with the §9 RC1 gate row and §1 O16
evidence.observation: §3 plans "| declared address | `src/gnd/address.py` (`declared_constraint_address`, moved from `coverage.py`) |" and O16 cites the existing implementation as "`coverage._constraint_address` (`src/gnd/coverage.py:735`)", but RC1's focused gate is "uv run pytest -q tests/test_rc1_*.py tests/test_schema_sync.py tests/test_checker_families.py tests/test_rf1_semantic_pins.py", which names no coverage suite, so the moved function's existing consumer is not exercised by the gate that authorises the move.

concerns.recommendation: Add the coverage suite that exercises `coverage._constraint_address` (and the `ModelIndex.iter_constraints()` walk rule 4 depends on) to RC1's gate in §9, or state that the move leaves a pinned re-export at the old call site; this seat reviewed inline bytes only and could not open src/gnd/coverage.py to identify the suite.
concerns.title: RC1 moves `coverage._constraint_address` into address.py without its consumer's tests in the focused gate

evidence.location: §2.1 first bullet, read with the §1 Issue 92 row, O2 and §4 RC1-C2
evidence.observation: Issue 92 gives "rule id and author message in each verdict" and O2 records that `constraint_common` "has `rationale`, no field for what to do", but §2.1 makes the new field optional ("`rationale` stays the reason the rule exists") and RC1-C2 accepts "`remedy` (null when undeclared)", so a model whose authors already wrote text only in `rationale` still yields a verdict carrying no author message.

concerns.recommendation: State in §2.1 whether the version-15 verdict also carries `rationale`, or record explicitly that `remedy: null` satisfies GR-D1 and that populating the field is the project owner's work, so RC1-C2's null case is a deliberate contract rather than an unstated gap for existing models.
concerns.title: GR-D1's author message reaches the verdict only for models that adopt the new optional field

response.summary: Reviewed the r2 plan bytes only, as this seat is instructed. Three blocking concerns: RC3-C4 asserts a violation-key stability under rule insertion that §2.3 and RC-D4 explicitly deny for positional addresses; RC4's 'payload records the option' has no named home while §3 declares RC4 independent of RC1, so the record can land in a variant rule 7 freezes; and the §5 claim that versions 3-14 keep their bytes has no criterion beyond the v7 rf1 goldens. Hardening concerns cover unnumbered time bounds resting on O15 (marked claim), the load-bearing redaction/temporal refusal that has no criterion and cites a nonexistent '(RC1 D3)', the unspecified --baseline x --allow-vacuous outcome although both phases edit band(), RC6 having neither budget nor resolved gate, RC1's gate having no recorded pre-change baseline against 24 failing tests, RC5-C2's 'one home' contradicting the §3 row that names two and omits the third spelling, the coverage.py move whose consumer tests are outside RC1's gate, and remedy being optional so existing rationale-only models still carry no author message. The obligations map covers O1-O17 and all five source requests, sequencing RC1->RC2->RC3 is sound, and O16/O17 are internally consistent; I could not open src/gnd/address.py, coverage.py or model_index.py to verify the cited line numbers because this seat reviews inline bytes only.
